english.text: "That story was so funny I literally died from laughter." "Then how come you're talking to me now?" "Of course, I didn't actually die, it was just a figure of speech." "So you're saying you used 'literally' in a figurative way." "Apparently. Got a problem with that?" "No, just finding it amusing that language can twist to the point that a word comes to mean its own opposite."

jyutping: 「go2 go3 gu3 si6 hou2 hou2 siu3，ngo5 zan1 hai6 siu3 dou3 sei2 zo2。」「gam2 dim2 gaai2 nei5 ji4 gaa1 tung4 ngo5 gong2 je5 aa3？」「dong1 jin4，ngo5 kei4 sat6 mou5 sei2，zi2 hai6 jat1 go3 bei2 jyu6。」「nei5 waa6 nei5 jung6 zo2「zi6 min2」hai6 bei2 jyu6 sing3 ge3 fong1 sik1。」「hou2 ming4 hin2。jau5 man6 tai4 maa5？」「m4 hai6，zi2 hai6 gok3 dak1 hou2 jau5 ceoi3，jyu5 jin4 ho2 ji5 nau2 kuk1 dou3 jat1 go3 zi6 ge3 ji3 si1 hai6 soeng1 faan2 ge3。」
text: 「嗰個故事好好笑，我真係笑到死咗。」「噉點解你而家同我講嘢呀？」「當然，我其實冇死，只係一個比喻。」「你話你用咗「字面」係比喻性嘅方式。」「好明顯。有問題嗎？」「唔係，只係覺得好有趣，語言可以扭曲到一個字嘅意思係相反嘅。」

english.text: America, we have come so far. We have seen so much. But there is so much more to do. So tonight, let us ask ourselves — if our children should live to see the next century; if my daughters should be so lucky to live as long as Ann Nixon Cooper, what change will they see? What progress will we have made? This is our chance to answer that call. This is our moment.
